title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Tb(III) and Dy(III) are the preferred lanthanide centers for high-performance rare-earth SMMs because strong 4f spin-orbit coupling makes the crystal field a perturbation and yields large single-ion anisotropy compared with early 3d cluster SMMs.
explanation: The review traces the shift from Mn12 and Fe clusters to lanthanide SMMs after 2003. It treats the first [TbPc2]- (Ueff about 331 cm^-1) as breaking the multinuclear 3d Ueff record and states that constructing SMMs from Tb and Dy remains an effective performance route, with LnPc complexes favored for spintronics.
scope: Mononuclear and polynuclear Ln-SMMs, especially phthalocyanine complexes of Tb and Dy.
conditions: Performance is discussed through Ueff and TB; TB is defined as the highest temperature at which magnetization hysteresis can be observed, subject to field sweep rate.
caveats: The review does not claim every Tb or Dy complex is an SMM; ligand-field geometry must still be optimized.
